//: The Worker's own tests: the three files under `_lib/` that
node runs directly, and the modules they import.
It is a config of its own because nothing else here is one.
`functions/` is compiled by wrangler's esbuild, which strips
types with no configuration and never reads a tsconfig, so a
`.ts` in this directory typechecks nowhere by default. That is
the trap `scripts/check-types.ts` was written for: node strips
the annotations without reading them, so a `.ts` nobody checks
is a `.js` wearing them. That check runs this config too.
Node and nothing else. No DOM, because none of this is a
browser: `fetch`, `Response`, `crypto.subtle`, `btoa` and
`TextEncoder` are globals @types/node carries, and the Worker
has the same ones. A test here that wanted a document would be
a test in the wrong directory.
`allowJs` stays OFF, which is the difference between this and
`scripts/tsconfig.json`. Inferring from an untyped `.js` is
how `any` gets in without anybody writing it, and there is no
longer a `.js` under `_lib/` for one of these to import: the
last hand-written declaration beside a module, `notion.d.ts`,
went when `notion.js` became `notion.ts` and started
describing itself.
`allowImportingTsExtensions` because that is how the imports
are written, `./quiz.ts` and `./sanitise.ts`, and they have to
be: node resolves the real filename and has no opinion about
what TypeScript would have preferred.
